verdict.reasoning: Patient reports symptoms for 'a few days' and doctor summarizes 'For the last four days, you've had very itchy skin, very sore skin...' and patient describes 'a sore, and a red skin... it's really itchy'.

Patient states rash is on 'my chest, my, my hands, my arms' and later clarifies 'Just the chest, hands and like, like inside the elbows.' When asked about the face, patient says 'On my face? No.' Antecubital fossae = inside the elbows.
Patient says 'I can't even sleep at night' and at work 'I can't focus... I'm always like, uh, disturbed by this disease,' indicating poor sleep and decreased concentration due to itch.
Patient reports 'I have to take like showers every day to be able to... ease this itching part,' indicating daily showers for pruritus relief.
Patient says 'my skin is a bit cracked in some parts' and denies discharge: 'No... you've not... seen any other pus or blood, coming out of your skin.'
When asked about fevers, patient responds 'No. just very itchy. Nothing else.'
Doctor asks 'Your chest is OK? No cough, no breathing difficulties?' and patient replies 'No.'
Patient: 'earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema' and later doctor summarizes 'your background of eczema.'
Patient: 'I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore.'
When asked about regular medications, patient replies 'Uh no.'
Patient: 'I bought a, a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night. But it apparently didn't help, because it's still itching a lot today.'

Patient describes prior treatment: 'they gave me like some cream, and something to, uh when I like shower... At that time yes... it did help,' indicating prior relief from topical cream and a bath/shower product.
Patient: 'Yes, I have tried antihistamines, uh lately, but it didn't really help.'
When asked 'do you have any allergies at all?' patient answers 'Uh, no.' This supports no known drug allergies.
Patient: 'I live with a few flatmates.'
Patient: 'I work uh at a pharmaceutical company... I'm a, like a kind of project manager.'
Doctor asks 'do you smoke at all?' and patient answers 'No.'
Patient: 'I'd say a few, a few beers per week. Something like this. Nothing, nothing crazy.'
Doctor states 'I do wonder whether this is a flare-up of your eczema. The reason being that you said it was quite itchy... having looked at your skin, uh the rash does appear quite familiar.'
Doctor: 'You mentioned using steroid creams, yesterday... I wonder whether giving you a stronger prescription of a of a steroid may be beneficial, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today.'

Doctor: 'I'm going to give you something, some emollients... which use in the bath and shower... it's definitely worth um using that for the first seven to ten days before we make the decision on whether it's working or not.'

Doctor advises 'using antihistamines... Things like Loratadine or Piriton, which can help the itchiness' and later 'I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well. Um, something like Fexofenadine, which I can give to you today.' (Piriton is chlorphenamine).

Doctor: 'it's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms, anything you wear or anything you use, in terms of shower gels or soap.' This is a trigger diary regarding products/clothing.
Doctor: 'do come back and see me next week, if things don't get better.'
